title: Audit Log Delivery SLO calcs (baseline + proposed thresholds)
content:
SRE working sheet for Audit Log Delivery SLO
Owner: Miles Thornton (SRE)
Last updated: 2025-06-18

Context
- Goal: define an SLO for audit event delivery lag (pipeline: ingest -> validate -> persist -> query API availability; and separately persist -> export -> sink ack).
- Non-negotiable: no sampling for audit logs (per Security). We treat “delay” vs “drop” separately.
- Metrics added in redwood/pr_18488. Dashboards/alerts drafted in observability-pack/pr_418.

Definitions (what we’re measuring)
1) delivery_lag_query_seconds
- For an emitted audit event, time from event.enqueued_at to event.persisted_at (i.e., queryable in audit log store / Audit Logs API).
- This is the primary “customer can see the log” measure.

2) delivery_lag_export_seconds (per sink)
- For export-enabled orgs, time from event.persisted_at to sink_ack_at.
- Separate because customers can self-diagnose their own sink issues, but we still need exporter SLO + paging.

3) drop_rate
- Events we accepted for processing but never persisted (or persisted but never exported after max retries) within a bounded window.
- Note: exporter DLQ counts as NOT dropped, but “export not completed”; we still page if DLQ rises above threshold.

TAB 1 — Baseline measurements (prod)
Data source: audit-log pipeline metrics + manual spot checks (2025-05-27 through 2025-06-10)
Notes:
- Excludes scheduled maintenance windows.
- Includes one known incident window (2025-06-03 exporter backlog) called out separately.

A) Query availability lag (enqueued -> persisted)
| Window | Region scope | p50 | p90 | p95 | p99 | max | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 2025-05-27..2025-06-02 | all | 1.8s | 4.9s | 8.7s | 23.4s | 71s | baseline pre-incident |
| 2025-06-03 (incident) | us-east + eu-west | 3.5s | 18s | 41s | 310s | 920s | exporter backlog spilled into persist lag due to queue contention (see thread_1717773314) |
| 2025-06-04..2025-06-10 | all | 1.9s | 5.2s | 9.1s | 28.6s | 88s | post-mitigation (scaled consumers + backlog drain) |

Observations:
- Normal-state p99 for query availability lag is < 30s.
- Tail risk: backlog + consumer starvation can push p99 into minutes; this is the failure mode we want to page on.

B) Export lag (persisted -> sink ack)
We measured S3 sink (majority), plus webhook (minority). Splunk HEC is still in limited beta.
| Sink type | p50 | p90 | p95 | p99 | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| S3 | 12s | 55s | 95s | 210s | dominated by batch flush interval + occasional AWS throttles |
| Webhook | 2s | 9s | 17s | 62s | dominated by customer endpoint response times |

Observations:
- Export lag is materially higher than persist lag for S3 (expected due to batching).
- Most customers care that logs are queryable quickly; exports can be slower but must be reliable and bounded.

TAB 2 — Expected load (events/sec) + headroom
Data source: last 14 days prod counts + growth assumptions (PM beta ramp + Dedicated/Private instrumentation).

Assumptions
- Current audit events cover ~65% of sensitive actions; project target is 100% coverage (expect event volume increase).
- Growth factor for “coverage completion” (not customer growth): +1.35x over 8 weeks.
- Customer growth (next 2 quarters): +1.25x (conservative, based on Hosted + Dedicated pipeline forecasts).
- Combined multiplier: 1.35 * 1.25 ≈ 1.69x

Current (observed)
| Metric | us-east-1 | eu-west-1 | ap-southeast-1 | total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Avg events/sec | 210 | 95 | 22 | 327 |
| Peak 5-min events/sec | 880 | 410 | 75 | 1,365 |
| Largest single-tenant peak (5-min) | 190 | 120 | 18 | 190 |

Projected (next 2 quarters)
| Metric | projection multiplier | projected avg events/sec | projected peak 5-min events/sec |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total | 1.69x | 553 | 2,306 |

Capacity notes (what we need to validate)
- Pipeline should sustain >2.5k events/sec total with <10s p95 persist lag.
- Exporter should handle burst flushes without blocking persist path (separate queues + backpressure).
- Biggest risk: a few orgs with export enabled generating a disproportionate share of events (e.g., CI automation around keys/RBAC). Need per-org fairness limits.

TAB 3 — Proposed SLOs
Primary SLO (Query availability)
- SLO name: Audit Log Query Availability Lag
- Objective: 99.9% of audit events are persisted (queryable via Audit Logs API) within 120 seconds, measured monthly.
- Measurement: ratio of events with delivery_lag_query_seconds <= 120 / total accepted events.
- Error budget: 0.1% per month.

Rationale
- Baseline p99 is ~30s; 120s gives headroom while still meaningful for incident response + compliance evidence.
- 120s keeps us honest on backlog scenarios without paging constantly for minor jitter.

Secondary SLO (Export completion, for export-enabled orgs)
- SLO name: Audit Log Export Completion Lag (per sink)
- Objective: 99% of persisted audit events are acknowledged by the configured sink within 300 seconds, measured monthly, excluding customer-caused webhook 5xx/timeout (tracked separately).
- Measurement: per-sink lag histogram; “customer-caused” classification requires exporter error taxonomy.

Drop SLO (non-negotiable)
- Objective: <= 0.001% dropped events (accepted but not persisted) per month.
- Objective: <= 0.01% export failures requiring DLQ (persisted but not delivered after max retries) per month.

Open question (needs Security sign-off)
- Do we want a stricter drop SLO for events classified as “critical” (RBAC/auth changes, key rotation, audit export config changes)? That would require event classification at emit-time.

TAB 4 — Alert thresholds (Grafana)
Dashboard links (internal)
- Grafana: Audit Logs / Delivery Overview: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/audit-log-delivery-overview
- Grafana: Audit Logs / Exporter Health: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/audit-log-exporter-health
- Grafana: Audit Logs / Queue & Consumer: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/audit-log-queue-consumers

Paging policy (prod)
A) Persist lag paging
- Page (P1): delivery_lag_query_seconds p99 > 300s for 5m AND accepted_events_rate > 50 events/sec
- Page (P1): persisted_events_rate / accepted_events_rate < 0.995 for 10m (sustained mismatch indicates drops or stuck consumers)
- Ticket (P2): delivery_lag_query_seconds p99 > 120s for 15m (early warning, should be investigated during business hours)

B) Exporter paging (per sink)
- Page (P1): export_backlog_events > 500k for 10m (backlog not draining)
- Page (P1): export_dlq_events increase rate > 100/min for 5m (systemic failures)
- Ticket (P2): delivery_lag_export_seconds p99 > 900s for 15m for S3 sink (likely AWS throttles or exporter contention)

C) Drop detection
- Page (P1): dropped_events_count > 0 (any) over 5m window for prod (audit logs are compliance-bound; any confirmed drop is an incident)
Notes:
- We need to be careful about false positives from metric gaps. Use “absent()” checks + alert on telemetry pipeline health.

TAB 5 — Backlog math / what triggers tail latency
Quick relationship (rule of thumb)
- If backlog grows by B events and steady-state drain rate is D events/sec, time-to-drain ≈ B / D seconds.
- Our p99 lag tends to correlate with backlog size and drain rate variability.

Example scenario (based on 2025-06-03 incident)
- Accepted rate during spike: ~1,400 events/sec
- Effective drain (persist) rate degraded to: ~900 events/sec (consumer saturation)
- Backlog growth: 500 events/sec
- After 30 minutes: B ≈ 500 * 1800 = 900,000 events
- Even if drain recovers to 1,500 events/sec with accepted back to 900 events/sec, net drain 600 events/sec => 900,000 / 600 ≈ 1,500s (~25 min) tail latency until fully drained.

Actionable
- Backpressure should preferentially shed export work before persist work.
- Consumer autoscaling needs to react within <5 minutes to backlog slope changes.

Notes / TODOs
- [TODO] Validate end-to-end measurement correctness: is enqueued_at always set at gateway edge? Any clock skew issues? (Caleb/Nadia)
- [TODO] Confirm exporter “customer-caused error” taxonomy + how it affects export SLO reporting (Svetlana + SRE)
- [TODO] Add per-org top talkers panel to Delivery Overview dashboard (helps with fairness + incident triage)
- [TODO] Decide whether to implement “critical event class” for stricter internal paging (Marcus Lin sign-off)

Change log
- 2025-05-22: initial baseline + draft SLO (Miles)
- 2025-06-05: added incident math + exporter lag baselines (Rafael)
- 2025-06-18: updated projections for 100% sensitive-action coverage (+1.35x) + customer growth (+1.25x); aligned paging thresholds with #eng-sre thread_1717510092 (Miles/Aisha)
